newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta minister encouraged toll deal - PanCanadian.
newsitem.headline: Alberta minister encouraged toll deal - PanCanadian.

text.p: A natural gas tolling deal between NOVA Corp and PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd was hammered out over the last week under the encouragement of Alberta's Energy Minister, a PanCanadian official said on Monday.
The deal effectively kills the threat to NOVA of a major pipeline competitor on its its traditional exclusive turf.

PanCanadian vice-president Gerry Protti said Alberta Energy Minister Pat Black had made it clear to the parties she wanted a deal reached commercially before the government or regulatory authorities were dragged into the emotional battle.
"That is what we have there," Protti said.
PanCanadian and NOVA unit NOVA Gas Transmission Ltd said on Monday they reached an agreement on tolls that should eliminate the need to construct the Palliser pipeline.

Under the deal, NOVA would establish a "load-retention rate" of C$0.155 per thousand cubic feet of gas transported on its system for eligible shippers who had executed precedent agreements with the proposed Palliser Pipeline.
The proposed rate would increase two percent per year for a 20-year term.

PanCanadian, along with partner Westcoast Energy Inc, had proposed the 1.2 billion cubic feet per day Palliser project because it believed it was paying tolls that were to high to transport its gas to the Alberta-Saskatchewan border.

Much of PanCanadian's gas production lies in the southern part of Alberta. But, under a traditional NOVA toll structure called the "postage stamp" rate, it paid the same amount to ship gas to the border as producers in the northernmost regions of the province.

Industry experts said on Monday that it remained to be seen what the response of northern producers would be to the NOVA-PanCanadian deal, which included a stipulation that NOVA would join PanCanadian in reviving Palliser if an application to Alberta's Energy and Utilities Board was unsuccessful.
The deal would see the postage stamp rate for other shippers raised by under a cent per thousand cubic feet from the current level of 26 cents.
"A penny's a penny, so it sets a precedent," said ScotiaMcleod pipeline analyst Sam Kanes.
"So, this precedent of economic differentials is going to open the box for things changing somewhat."
A NOVA official said the agreement could spell the end of NOVA's postage stamp tolls, which had been lauded as responsible for the development of remote gas fields.

"To the extent that this opens the door for alternate pricing structures over the long term may well lead to an evolution in the postage stamp tolling methodology," said NOVA vice-president Eric Shelton.
NOVA spokesman Paul Clark said the company could offer lower costs to all producers with the deal, something that would have been impossible with Palliser in place.
Kanes said the deal was "a mild favorable" for NOVA shareholders because itss core pipeline network would remain whole, assuming there were no challenges to the agreement.

Protti, who said the pact was hammered out using the services of a mediator, said he expected PanCanadian to use the funds that had been earmarked for the project on a greatly expanded exploration and production program.
